title: Colour grading in the mixer
objective: Extend the existing mixer with Lightroom-familiar tonal and Global grading, shared atomic wheels and numeric/API parity, independently proven CPU/GPU rendering, masks, presets and mapped Lightroom grading documents.
context_summary: The owner settled product choices on 2026-10-07 and requested an implementation-ready plan with no approval/research gates. Deliver HSL/Grading tabs with three-way and individual/Global wheels, luminance, masks, Luxforge presets and direct Lightroom preset mappings; retain dormant hue and scoped resets. Initial numerical/layout details are implementer decisions. TASK-001 records the completed contract. TASK-002 and TASK-003 implement numerics and shared controls immediately; TASK-009 hands off the working feature. Only TASK-010 performs independent f64 reference analysis and Lightroom matching/refinement, with no dependency back into initial delivery. Lightroom exports are measurement inputs, not approval gates or prerequisites for feature/tooling implementation. Ordinary correctness tests, GPU-versus-CPU checks and background rendered evidence ship with the feature. Keep current shapes only, bounded work and the roadmap high-tier minimum.

tasks.description: Implement the initial bounded grading colour unit and its correctness fixtures.
extra_context: Implement production numerical behaviour now; there is no independent study, Lightroom data or owner contact-sheet prerequisite. Select/document initial equations and constants through engineering judgement within the settled design.

Use post-HSL perceptual brightness, smooth three-range weights, Balance/Blending, RGB-wheel hue-to-tint conversion, luminance and independent Global composition. Oklab is the initial candidate; handle signed/headroom RAW explicitly and retain alpha.

Keep this outcome independent of the payload declaration: the unit consumes fixed typed coefficients/parameters for the fourteen decided fields. TASK-004 binds it to the API, and TASK-005 ports the same contract to the GPU.

Add ordinary whole-buffer/neutral/finite/continuity tests for the chosen initial equations. Independent f64 analysis, response plots, Lightroom matching and perfection belong exclusively to TASK-010 after delivery.

tasks.description: Add semantic hue/saturation wheel and nested view controls through the shared UI paths.
extra_context: The frozen parameter and interaction contract comes from the completed TASK-001; numerical grading output is not needed to implement and prove the controls. Exercise the controls proof module before mixer integration.

A grading-only measurement path is reusable/tested on known synthetic responses, writes only round-owned copies/evidence and consumes actual Lightroom exports without a private catalog.

Available Lightroom inputs produce scoped response/residual figures and warranted B/C changes; when unavailable, figures stay explicitly unmeasured rather than becoming an approval or feature-delivery gate.
Any numerical/conversion changes receive exact fixture, native GPU-versus-reference and rendered checks, with current format refusal and updated docs; alignment claims never exceed the measurements.
The final reference/tooling outcome is delivered autonomously, with no dependency back into TASK-009 and no new product-approval task.

steps: Run targeted independent-reference and known-response measurement tests; inspect generated manifests and source preservation.
Consume available Lightroom exports and review response plots/contact sheets as implementer work; accurately report missing measured inputs.
For numerical refinements, run targeted CPU/GPU comparisons, affected background smoke and rendered verification; run quick once at the completed handoff.
expected_results: Reference analysis and calibration tooling are delivered after the working feature; measured matching is reported only where actual exports support it.
